content.title: About
content.content: Red raw onions are fresh onion bulbs with a vivid red hue and a milder, slightly sweet flavor compared to typical yellow onions. They are commonly used in salads, salsas, and as a colorful garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red onions contain higher levels of anthocyanins, which give them their distinctive color and act as antioxidants.
They originated from selective breeding of yellow onions but have a higher sugar content, making them less pungent.
In some cuisines they are used as a natural food coloring.
When stored for a long time the bright color can fade, turning a more pinkish hue.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and quercetin help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Sulfur compounds can lower cholesterol levels and improve vascular tone.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: May help regulate blood sugar
items.content: Flavonoids and fiber slow glucose absorption, beneficial for pre‑diabetic individuals.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber and prebiotic compounds promote healthy gut bacteria.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to onions, ranging from skin rashes to severe symptoms.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Raw onions can aggravate heartburn and irritate the stomach lining in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Odor and gas
items.content: Sulfur compounds cause the characteristic smell and may lead to flatulence and bad breath.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Red raw onions are often sliced thinly or diced and added to salads, sandwiches, guacamole, and marinades. They can be lightly pickled in vinegar or lemon juice to soften the bite.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store onions in a cool, dry, dark place in a mesh bag. For longer freshness, keep them in the refrigerator where they stay good for 2–3 weeks. Keep them away from potatoes, as they accelerate each other's spoilage.
